findings.issue: The '20% / one in five fail in year one' figure is consistent with multiple UK sources (ONS business demography data, FSB reports, independent aggregators). Some sources put it slightly lower or higher depending on methodology and year. The claim is a widely accepted general statistic, not fabricated, and is not attributed to a specific named study with a specific year, so the risk of a mark-affecting error is negligible.
findings.correct_version: No change needed — the statistic is broadly accurate and consistent with published UK business failure data.

findings.lesson_title: Advertising, Sales Promotion and Public Relations
findings.claim_text: TV adverts are a named medium in the specification, added to the list in 2025.
findings.issue: CONFIRMED ACCURATE. The OCR specification amendment page (ocr.org.uk/administration/support-and-tools/subject-updates/cambridge-nationals-spec-amends-742508/) confirms that 'TV advert' was added as a type of non-digital advertising medium to R067 Topic Area 4.3, published 9 September 2025 and updated 17 September 2025. The lesson's statement that this happened 'in 2025' is correct. The resulting count of seven non-digital mediums (leaflets, newspapers, magazines, radio, billboards, cinema, TV) is also confirmed accurate — TV was added to a pre-existing six-medium list. No error.
findings.correct_version: No change needed — claim is accurate and verified against the official OCR amendment page.

findings.lesson_title: Business Ownership and Sources of Capital
findings.claim_text: A private limited company (Ltd) requires formal registration with Companies House, and annual accounts are filed publicly.
findings.issue: CONFIRMED ACCURATE on both counts. Gov.uk and Companies House confirm that (1) all private limited companies must register with Companies House, and (2) annual accounts filed with Companies House are public records accessible by anyone. No error.
findings.correct_version: No change needed — claim is accurate.

findings.lesson_title: Business Ownership and Sources of Capital
findings.claim_text: Sole trader: 'There is no formal registration process beyond informing tax authorities.'
findings.issue: Technically, registering for Self Assessment with HMRC is a legal requirement for sole traders earning over £1,000. However, the lesson's framing aligns with how the R067 spec itself distinguishes sole trader set-up (lighter HMRC notification) from private limited company registration (formal Companies House incorporation). The lesson is not saying registration is optional — it explicitly says 'beyond informing tax authorities', which is the HMRC Self Assessment step. The contrast being drawn is accurate: sole traders do NOT register with Companies House, unlike Ltd companies. This is a spec-level teaching distinction rather than a factual error. No mark-affecting error.
findings.correct_version: No change needed — the distinction from Ltd registration is pedagogically correct and aligns with the R067 specification's intended contrast.

findings.claim_text: The Chamber of Commerce is a membership organisation for local businesses providing networking events, training sessions, business advice workshops, and advocacy.
findings.issue: CONFIRMED ACCURATE. The British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) website confirms this is an accurate description. Chambers provide networking events, advocacy to government, training, and business support. No error.

findings.claim_text: Government grants do not have to be repaid, but they are competitive, often come with conditions on how the money is spent, and are not guaranteed.
findings.issue: CONFIRMED ACCURATE. This is a standard and correct description of government business grants in the UK. Gov.uk and British Business Bank sources confirm grants are non-repayable but competitive and conditional. No error.

summary.notes: This is a clean set of 12 lessons. The content uses fictional business scenarios throughout (Millbrook Candle Co., Floret Skincare, Ferndale, Priya's plant service, etc.) and avoids naming real companies in ways that would invite fabrication. The three LOW findings are all confirmed accurate on verification — they are flagged only because they touched verifiable spec claims or regulatory facts that warranted checking. The most important verification was the L8 claim that TV adverts were 'added to the specification in 2025', which is confirmed by the official OCR amendment page published September 2025. No errors were found that would affect students' exam preparation or that would be considered mark-affecting.
